name: Satia Industries Ltd
tagline: Integrated agri-residue writing-&-printing-paper maker with captive pulp + power and state-textbook contracts that smooth the cycle — cheap on EV/EBITDA at a cycle trough, but structurally challenged demand, zero-duty ASEAN imports, no growth capex and a related private paper company
business_overview: Manufacturer of writing & printing (W&P) paper from wood and agricultural residue, with captive pulping and captive (co-generation) power; a large share of output is supplied to state education boards on contracts that delay raw-material price pass-through in both directions. Also small agriculture and power-cogeneration lines.
fundamentals_table: EV/EBITDA ~2-5x on FY24-TTM — among the cheapest listed paper stocks
Depreciation ~20% of gross block (vs ~5-9% at JK Paper / West Coast / Seshasayee) — a large drag on reported PAT
~96% on PM4; ~3 years to add new capacity; no major growth capex planned
fundamentals_narrative: Satia is a well-integrated, low-cost W&P paper maker that has held margins better than peers through the down-cycle (state-textbook contracts, captive pulp/power, agri-residue fuel). It is genuinely cheap — EV/EBITDA ~2-5x, low price-to-book at a cyclical trough (ROCE ~4%). But the sector faces structural demand pressure (digitisation) and a 43%+ surge in zero-duty ASEAN/FTA imports; the New Education Policy textbook demand that could offset this has been repeatedly delayed by publishers; management has no meaningful growth capex and guides only 5-10% volume growth; depreciation runs ~20% of gross block, heavily suppressing PAT; and a promoter-linked private company (Satia Paper Mills Pvt Ltd, same business, same town) plus promoter-linked public shareholders were flagged by an elevated user as a governance watch-item (unresolved, 2023).
sentiment_summary: Well-covered historically (elevated users Rafi_Syed, dineshssairam, lohiyaakshay08, thakurvi). The debate is 'cheap trough cyclical / possible P/E re-rating' vs 'no growth plan, structural headwinds, why re-rate'. Thread has gone quiet since 2024 (one Sep-2026 post sharing a third-party case study). dineshssairam's Satia-Paper-Mills-Pvt-Ltd governance question (2023, well-received) remains unanswered.
community_signal: No current trusted 'buy' call; the historical trusted view is 'cheap but needs growth or a re-rating catalyst that hasn't come'. Discovery candidate, theme-rank 2 (no live-theme keyword match).
key_new_facts: ROCE/ROE at ~4% — a cyclical trough; EV/EBITDA ~2-5x, among the cheapest paper stocks.
Depreciation ~20% of gross block (peers ~5-9%) — large structural drag on reported PAT.
~96% utilisation, ~3 years to add capacity, no major growth capex; management guides only 5-10% volume growth.
Zero-duty ASEAN/FTA paper imports up 43%+ (uncoated W&P up sharply) — a persistent margin headwind; NEP textbook demand repeatedly delayed.
Unresolved governance watch-item: Satia Paper Mills Pvt Ltd (promoter-linked, same business/town) plus promoter-linked public shareholders.
bull_case: Cheapest listed W&P paper stock on EV/EBITDA, at a cycle trough; held margins better than peers in the down-cycle
Integrated: captive pulp, captive power, agri-residue fuel; state-textbook contracts smooth volumes
Optionality on a paper-price up-cycle and NEP textbook demand + possible P/E re-rating
bear_case: Structurally challenged demand (digitisation) + surging zero-duty FTA imports
No growth capex, ~96% utilised, only 5-10% volume growth guided
Depreciation ~20% of gross block crushes reported PAT; ROCE ~4%
Related promoter-owned private paper company (Satia Paper Mills Pvt Ltd) — unresolved governance question
verdict_headline: Cheap, well-integrated trough-cycle paper stock with structural demand headwinds, no growth capex and a related private paper company — 'neither', Low-Medium conviction
verdict_reasoning: Discovery candidate, theme-rank 2 (no live-theme keyword match — recency discovery).

four_box score 2.0 (tailwind no — W&P paper demand structurally pressured, zero-duty FTA imports surging, NEP offset delayed; tam weak — ~96% utilised, ~3 yrs to add capacity, only 5-10% volume growth guided; moat weak — captive pulp/power + textbook contracts are a cost edge, not pricing power; valuation yes — EV/EBITDA ~2-5x at a cyclical trough). Valuation box is 'yes' so a return-magnitude label is technically permitted (exception), but the honest maths for a trough paper cyclical is ~2-3x on a cycle turn + re-rating, not 10x/100x -> thesis_fit stays 'neither'.
Governance: the Satia Paper Mills Pvt Ltd relationship is a soft, unresolved watch-item flagged by an elevated user, not a red_flag_tier event — no SEBI order, no going concern.
Conviction Low-Medium: genuinely cheap and well-run at a trough, but structural demand headwinds, no growth plan and the related-party shade keep it a watch, not a buy. First-time read.

value_chain.position: low-cost integrated W&P paper maker; large state-textbook supply share
value_chain.bottleneck_node: none structural — FTA imports set the price ceiling; captive pulp/power is a cost buffer
value_chain.note: Domestic W&P capacity has been rationalising, but zero-duty ASEAN/Korea/Japan imports cap pricing; Satia's edge is cost integration and textbook contracts, not a moat that supports a large re-rating.
